Segment.divide cuts each segment once at every cut inside it, so wrapping a long line is linear in its length (rich-unfiled-791c.vzmy)

cutCells takes every position in one walk; Segment.cutAt applies it with each
piece's anchor shifted, and splitCells is its one-cut case. The Markdown
linearity guards now time drawing, not only reading.

Markdown measures a list item's line under a `>` from that line's own quote, as markdown-it does (rich-unfiled-791c.jlk3) (#465)

* Markdown measures a list item's line under a `>` from that line's own quote, as markdown-it does (rich-unfiled-791c.jlk3)

markdown-it's listIndent and sCount count from each line's own quote content.
A line short of an item took the marker line's margin as an absolute column,
so a `>` at another column read as lazy text: "> -    a\n    > - b" drew one
item "a - b" where Rich draws two. ItemStart now carries `listIndent`, the
container's margin past the marker line's quote content, and a short line
adds it to its own `quoteStart`.

Keeping the short line's own margin instead fixes this shape but breaks
nested lists whose line is lazy to an outer item; the last case in the test
pins that.

Differential against markdown-it-py on 60k random quote/list/table inputs:
0 regressions, 5 fixed, none left differing outside tables.

* Markdown's Line and ItemStart docs say which frame a list container's margin is counted in (rich-unfiled-791c.jlk3)
